_meta.purpose: Per-family Codex translation applied on top of the frozen OpenClaw design inventory to produce codex-matrix.json. Fields not listed here are inherited unchanged (title, scenarios, intervention, oracle, controls, evidence, metrics, coverage, billing). Scenario overrides must preserve the original scenario count. Mechanisms are rewritten for every family; other fields are overridden only where the original text names OpenClaw-specific surfaces.

REL-01.mechanism: A turn accepted by the app-server thread and its rollout JSONL record in the owned CODEX_HOME can be committed at different times.
REL-01.intervention: Inject termination at instrumented boundaries; distinguish a turn acknowledged as persisted from a merely received request.
REL-01.oracle: Compare acknowledged turn IDs with rollout records and completed work after restarting the app-server and resuming the thread; report the unacknowledged ambiguity window separately.
scenarios: after rollout append but before turn completion notification
after completion notification but before any dependent effect

REL-02.mechanism: An external effect committed by a sandboxed command and the turn's completion acknowledgment can be committed at different times.

REL-03.mechanism: A forked thread and the shared app-server daemon can both act as continuation owners of the same thread at different times.
REL-03.intervention: Terminate or partition the owning client, daemon and forked thread independently; allow a stale owner to publish after reassignment.
REL-03.oracle: Track thread ownership, resumed turns, accepted results and effect IDs in an independent ledger; a stale owner's result must not silently overwrite the current owner's result.

REL-04.mechanism: Whether execution continues after the codex process exits, the app-server daemon restarts, or a turn stops depends on separate persistence and ownership paths.
REL-04.intervention: Terminate only the identified codex process, app-server daemon or plugin/MCP host; keep an unrelated thread active.
REL-04.oracle: Record which threads stop and which resume automatically; availability, recovery correctness, and required human work remain separate outcomes.

REL-05.mechanism: turn/interrupt must propagate to queued turns, running sandboxed commands, background child processes and resumable checkpoints.
REL-05.intervention: Cancel at each execution boundary with turn/interrupt and command/exec/terminate, then inspect all descendant processes and externally observable effects.

REL-06.mechanism: Thread identity lives in rollout files, session_index.jsonl and the SQLite state inside CODEX_HOME; relocating any subset can split identity.

REL-07.mechanism: A working environment is reconstructed from repository-owned config.toml, auth inputs, MCP registrations and skills alone, without host state leakage.

REL-08.mechanism: Path, Unicode, cancellation and state-import semantics differ between the Linux sandbox and other platforms; only Linux arms are scheduled in this campaign.

REL-09.mechanism: Provider endpoints and credentials are read from model_providers config and auth storage; rebinding them exercises reconnection and re-auth.

REL-10.mechanism: A consistent backup of the owned CODEX_HOME must capture rollout files and SQLite databases while turns are active.

REL-11.mechanism: Thread-history migration (codex migrate-rollouts) and binary upgrades change persisted state in steps that can be interrupted.
scenarios: after migration commit before the new version is ready

REL-12.mechanism: Plugin and MCP registrations are republished and repaired through plugin/reconcile and config/mcpServer/reload without host state.

REL-13.mechanism: MCP client sessions in rmcp-client have lifetimes and cancellation semantics independent of the MCP server process.

REL-14.mechanism: Responses-API streaming carries fragmented tool-call arguments, usage and opaque reasoning fields that must round-trip through the native client.

REL-15.mechanism: Provider failures (rate limits, 5xx, connection loss, deadlines, fallback, context limits) are retried on the real request path with bounded behavior.

SEC-01.mechanism: Execution authority is projected from SandboxMode, execpolicy rules and approval flows onto shell commands, file changes, MCP tools and plugins.

SEC-02.mechanism: Credentials from auth storage and provider env keys propagate to sandboxed commands and MCP servers with distinct lifetimes.

SEC-03.mechanism: Sandbox setup enforces writable roots and network policy; setup failures and path races change the enforced boundary.

SEC-04.mechanism: Threads in one CODEX_HOME share persistence but must not share authority.
SEC-04.intervention: Run two synthetic tenants concurrently, restart shared MCP hosts, and attempt cross-thread reads or credential reuse.

SEC-05.mechanism: Effective policy is resolved from config.toml, -c overrides, profiles and app-server config writes at supported entry points.
SEC-05.intervention: Identify Codex policy sources and mandatory versus optional configuration, then vary one layer across supported entry points.

SEC-06.mechanism: Approval server requests (command execution, patch application, file change, permissions) and actual dispatch are separate steps.

SEC-07.mechanism: OAuth grants for the account, gateway and MCP servers are obtained, refreshed and revoked through distinct native flows.

SEC-08.mechanism: User content persists in rollout files, history, logs and exports; deletion and redaction act on each sink separately.

SEC-09.mechanism: Untrusted instructions can arrive through retrieved content, tool results, repository files, skills and memory.

SEC-10.mechanism: Network egress is controlled by sandbox policy and the network-proxy component under the declared sandbox modes.

SEC-11.mechanism: The app-server daemon control socket and remote-control transport authenticate clients before control-plane access.
SEC-11.title: App-server and control-plane authentication

SEC-12.mechanism: Plugins and marketplace entries are installed and updated from untrusted sources with manifest-declared capabilities.

PERF-01.mechanism: Turn preparation (history assembly, tool catalogue, caches) sits on the response path before model dispatch.

PERF-02.mechanism: CPU-bound preparation and asynchronous waiting contribute differently to turn latency.
PERF-02.intervention: Use controlled CPU-bound preparation and IO-wait fixtures in the pinned Codex runtime; vary supported execution placement while preserving the task result.

PERF-03.mechanism: Tool scheduling and state-writer locks serialize concurrent operations across threads and commands.

PERF-04.mechanism: A slow turn or tool call can delay unrelated short requests through shared scheduling or state paths.

PERF-05.mechanism: Admission under sustained, burst and overload conditions is governed by thread concurrency and the queue database.

PERF-06.mechanism: Parallel sessions contend on SQLite state and thread-writer locks inside CODEX_HOME.

PERF-07.mechanism: Codex exposes cloud tasks and an exec-server rather than a self-hosted node-dispatch contract; multi-host applicability must be probed at the pinned commit.
PERF-07.oracle: Verify placement of the model loop, state owner, tools, and result commit; mark unavailable hosts as untested rather than simulating a claim. If the pinned Codex deployment does not advertise self-hosted multi-host execution, record unsupported with a capability probe and the pinned support contract; do not simulate support with a harness-owned second service.

PERF-08.mechanism: Sustained load and recycling exercise queue stability, memory slope and state growth over bounded durations.

PERF-09.mechanism: Task-solving ability on independently accepted deliverables is measured with the pinned real model through the native provider path.

PERF-10.mechanism: Long conversations exceed context limits and trigger native compaction (thread/compact/start) with measurable completion effects.

COST-01.mechanism: Resident memory has an idle baseline and a marginal cost per active thread and session.

COST-02.mechanism: Initialization cost amortizes across cold process starts, warm daemon reuse and plugin or skill loading.

COST-03.mechanism: Context and memory features amortize token and time cost across later tasks when they work as declared.

COST-04.mechanism: Disk and inode usage amplify through rollout files, SQLite databases and cached artifacts.

COST-05.mechanism: No native concurrent-execution budget is advertised at this commit; account rate limits are not local budgets.
COST-05.oracle: Probe the pinned runtime for a native shared execution or token budget mechanism. If absent, record unsupported with a capability probe and the pinned support contract, exactly like the OpenClaw campaign; do not treat harness-side limits as product budgets.

COST-06.mechanism: Detailed hardware accounting covers processes, memory, disk, IO, network and cleanup completeness for owned runs.

COST-07.mechanism: Provider usage reported by responses and account/usage/read must reconcile with the independent request ledger.

EXT-01.mechanism: Extensions (plugins, MCP servers, skills) can be replaced while threads are active.

EXT-02.mechanism: Provider routing through model_providers and external harness use through codex mcp are alternative integration depths.

EXT-03.mechanism: Plugin manifests and skills declare versioned interfaces; old artifacts must load on new binaries.

EXT-04.mechanism: Context maintenance (compaction, context fragments, message history) is a component contract affecting continuation.

EXT-05.mechanism: MCP transports (stdio, Streamable HTTP) and content types must round-trip through the native MCP client.

EXT-06.mechanism: AGENTS.md discovery and Skill packages feed instructions with precedence and path rules.

EXT-07.mechanism: External tools, plugins and harnesses integrate through the plugin system, skill packages and MCP configuration.
EXT-07.intervention: Use a declared external artifact corpus and identify the documented Codex integration route required by each artifact.

EXT-08.mechanism: Plugin hooks run in declared order and may mutate inputs or outputs or fail; the supported hook set is enumerated by hooks/list.
EXT-08.intervention: Register local reference hooks through documented Codex plugin interfaces and inspect actual invocation events and downstream effects.

EXT-09.mechanism: Multiple plugins coexist through public manifest APIs without core edits or private imports.

OBS-01.mechanism: Authorization decisions (approvals, execpolicy verdicts) are recorded in thread items and logs with actor attribution.

OBS-02.mechanism: Diagnostic events export through the OTEL pipeline whose durability differs from canonical rollout state.

OBS-03.mechanism: Blind diagnosis reconstructs known injected faults from accessible records alone.

OBS-04.mechanism: Retention, export and modification boundaries apply to rollout, history and log records.

OBS-05.mechanism: Operational diagnosis uses codex doctor and codex debug on injected fault classes.

OBS-06.mechanism: Open trajectories link model requests, tool calls, hook activity and effects through rollout records and server notifications.

OBS-07.mechanism: Practical trace access and export support defect diagnosis through rollout-trace and debug tooling.
